tool_input.command: git stash push app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts -q && bun test tests/PostUpdate.test.ts 2>&1 | tail -5; git stash pop -q; git diff --stat

result:
Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 6/6.

I fixed `PostController.update` in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:88-99`, which was taking the raw request JSON and writing it with `Post.forceUpdate` — bypassing both validation and the model's mass-assignment allowlist. It now runs the body through `this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` (the same schema `store` and the `posts.update` route already use, so an invalid `title`/`excerpt`/`body` is refused with a 422 and field errors before anything is written) and applies it with `Post.update`, which enforces `Post.fillable = ['title', 'excerpt', 'body']`; `authorId` sits deliberately outside that allowlist and is stripped by the schema, so request input can no longer reassign a post's author, and unknown fields like `createdAt` are dropped rather than written. Authorization ordering is unchanged, so non-authors still get a 403. I also added `tests/PostUpdate.test.ts`, a feature test that migrates the test database, creates an author, a bystander and a post, and covers the four rules from the report: an `authorId` in the body is ignored, out-of-form fields are not written, an empty title yields 422 with the post untouched, and a non-author edit is refused with 403 — I verified all three new assertions fail against the pre-fix controller.
